# Diamond Prajna Paramita Sutra

<meta>continues from previous page: "...because he does not enter into"</meta> form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or phenomena <gloss>dharmas</gloss>; this is why he is called a <term>Srotaapanna</term> <gloss>Stream-enterer</gloss>.

"What do you think? Can a <term>Sakadagamin</term> <gloss>Once-returner</gloss> give rise to the thought: 'I have attained the fruit of a <term>Sakadagamin</term>'?"

<term>Subhuti</term> replied, "No, <term>Bhagavan</term> <gloss>World-Honored One</gloss>. Why is this? The <term>Sakadagamin</term> is named for returning once, but in reality, there is no such thing as going or coming. Therefore, he is named a <term>Sakadagamin</term>."

"Subhuti, what do you think? Can an <term>Anagamin</term> <gloss>Non-returner</gloss> give rise to the thought: 'I have attained the fruit of an <term>Anagamin</term>'?"

<term>Subhuti</term> replied, "No, <term>Bhagavan</term> <gloss>World-Honored One</gloss>. Why is this? The <term>Anagamin</term> is named for not returning, but in reality, there is no such thing as not returning. Therefore, he is named an <term>Anagamin</term>."

<summary>This page explores the second and third stages of Buddhist enlightenment, the Once-returner and the Non-returner. It emphasizes that these designations are nominal labels because the practitioners do not perceive themselves as having attained a fixed or inherent state.</summary>
<keywords>Srotaapanna, Sakadagamin, Anagamin, Subhuti, Diamond Sutra, emptiness, enlightenment stages</keywords>
